p.i: Hæc cœna tuta est, hanc tibi dedico

main_text.head: Ad Bibliothecam Reuerendiss. D. Theodori Bezæ.

p.i: MAgni Bibliotheca docta Bezæ, Quo nil candidius, disertiusque Nil concinnius, eruditiusque Phœbi suspiciunt nouem sorores, Et iunctus Charitum Lepos corea, Paucos, si superest locus, libellos, (Quod paruum tibi dedicare munus Audax me mea nunc iubet Thalia) Inis scriniolis, precor, reponas? Nec tradas Domino statim legendos: Sed quando grauibus licebit illum Curis cernere liberum, atque honesta Quærentem recreatione longum Musa fallere tadium seuera. Tunc, tunc, fida Velim roges Patronam Nostris otia commodet Camœnis: Quas si fronte leget seréniore Non Vulgi metuent procaciores Linguas, nec tenues erunt cululli Vendentis calidum piper taberna.

page.notes: Top line of the first stanza is partly damaged; the first line reads "Pifces Lemannus quos aluit sinu," as far as legible. Small ink marks and stains on the page are not transcribed. Some letters in the poem are doubtful, notably "Lemannus", "cululli" and "Inis" (possibly "Inis" for "In his"), and are reproduced as printed.
